obligations.text: A release run publishes only from an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag that verifies against `tools/rustev-release/allowed_signers`, whose commit is reachable from `main`, carries a successful `ci-gate`, and whose release set's version is `X.Y.Z`; any other ref publishes nothing.

A rerun never publishes different bytes: a crate, npm package or release asset already public at the version is skipped when its registry checksum equals the run's verified artifact, and fails the run otherwise; nothing is yanked, unpublished or replaced.

No tag, signature, attestation, Environment approval, registry state, manifest or qualification verdict produced by the release is an authorization accepted by any action executor; they are release evidence only (spec 001, 031 3.13).

One workflow run builds every release artifact once from the tagged commit, builds each a second time on independent runners and requires identical bytes before any publication; no artifact is taken from another run.

The release manifest and `SHA256SUMS` are generated by the run from the artifacts it built and verified, and receive the same SLSA build provenance attestation as every artifact; neither is an input to the run.

Crates are published to crates.io and npm packages to the npm registry from the run through trusted publishing (OIDC), npm packages with provenance; no long-lived registry token is read when trusted publishing is configured.

The run's last stage is the fresh-consumer qualification of 021 3.10 and 031 3.9.7 against the public registries and the GitHub release it created; its failure fails the run and leaves the lifecycle at `released`.

sectionHeadings: 058: One tagged run releases the family (amends 021, 031, 053 and 056)
record.summary: A proposed amendment of approved specs 021 (3.1, 3.8 to 3.10), 031 (3.9, 3.11, 3.12), 053 and 056 (3.3 to 3.5), modeled on spec-spine's tag-gated release. Pushing the owner's signed annotated tag `vX.Y.Z` on a commit of `main` starts one workflow run that builds every artifact once, checks reproducibility inside the run, generates and attests the manifest from what it built, publishes crates and npm packages through trusted publishing, creates and verifies the GitHub release, and ends with the fresh-consumer qualification. The rehearsal precondition, the owner-signed manifest, the second run, the signed publication instruction and its journal continuation are removed; release candidates become optional. Ratified by the owner on 2026-10-28 (A-61): the signed tag alone authorizes a release, and crates.io is published through trusted publishing.
record.title: One tagged run releases the family (amends 021, 031, 053 and 056)
